feedback: Pre-race review. Nothing has raced for this candidate, so this states no outcome for it. The candidate is valid: five sensors match five weights, all x-positions are within ±0.08 m, and base_speed 1.5 is inside its 0.05 to 2 range. It changes one field from the best raced design (iteration 7, score 42.8697): controller.base_speed from 1.4 to 1.5, with geometry (outer ±0.07, inner ±0.03, centre 0), weights, kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.2 and line_loss last_direction unchanged. The evidence for speed is the strongest lever measured so far. Iteration 6 showed base_speed 1.2 cut oval progress from 0.213 to 0.124 with s-bend and slalom flat, and iterations 3 to 5 moved kp, ki and kd by under 0.5 in total. Speed is the one lever with a large measured effect on the oval, which carries most of the score. Iteration 7 also showed line_loss_events of 0.6 per run on the oval, so the risk here is that higher speed raises slip and line loss on the oval. Watch line_loss_events and max_error together. Do not treat the rationale's expected progress gains as measured. After the race, use the telemetry as follows. (a) If oval progress rises above 0.226 with line_loss_events at or below 0.6 and the s-bend and slalom progress near 0.042 and 0.037, keep 1.5 and consider a single further step to 1.6 next. (b) If line_loss_events rises above 0.6 or oval progress falls below 0.226, return base_speed to 1.4 (iteration 7), since it is the best raced design. (c) If max_error stays at about 0.0622 with progress flat on every track, speed is not the limit and the next test should be a single sensing or controller field, not more speed. Change one group of fields per revision.
requested_changes: After the race, if oval progress rises above iteration 7's 0.2261 and line_loss_events stays at or below 0.6, keep controller.base_speed at 1.5 and consider 1.6 in a later iteration, with all other fields unchanged.
If line_loss_events rises above iteration 7's 0.6 on the oval, or oval progress falls below 0.2261, set controller.base_speed back to 1.4, since iteration 7 is the best raced design at 42.8697.

If max_error stays at about 0.0622 with flat progress on every track, do not raise speed further; test one controller field in isolation (for example kp from 2.5 to 2.0) with the iteration 7 geometry, citing iterations 3 to 5 where gain changes moved the score by under 0.5.
